## Peer-reviewed publication

::: {.pub-card}
**A Novel Architecture Optimization Using Deep Learning for Alzheimer's
Multiclass Disease Detection**

Z. Fatima, I. Noreen, R. Butt, **M. F. Chaudhary**

*Journal of Information Communication Technologies and Robotic Applications
(JICTRA)*, vol. 17, no. 1, June 2026 · Original article · CC BY-NC 4.0

[DOI: 10.51239/jictra.v17i1.363](https://doi.org/10.51239/jictra.v17i1.363) ·
[Article page](https://www.jictra.com.pk/index.php/jictra/article/view/363) ·
[PDF](https://www.jictra.com.pk/index.php/jictra/article/view/363/182)
:::

**Problem.** Alzheimer's disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) are
easiest to treat when caught early, but MRI-based deep-learning classifiers
struggle with the task: the stages look alike on a scan, labelled data is
scarce, and convolutional networks overfit easily.

**What we did.** We trained convolutional neural networks to classify brain
MRI scans into four stages (non-demented, very mild, mild and moderate
dementia) on the Kaggle Augmented Alzheimer dataset. Rather than proposing
one fixed network, we optimised the architecture: eleven CNN variants were
compared while tuning the learning rate, batch size, dropout rate and
optimiser (Adam, AdamW, SGD) in an ablation study.

**Result.** The best configuration reached **90.6 % accuracy, 96 %
specificity and a 90 % F1-score**. The high specificity matters clinically:
few healthy patients are wrongly flagged.

**My contribution.** The paper grew out of my Bachelor's final-year project at
Bahria University (see below), which I designed and implemented: the CNN
pipeline, the optimiser ablation and the hyperparameter search.

**Keywords:** Alzheimer's disease · Mild Cognitive Impairment · convolutional
neural networks · deep learning · hyperparameter optimisation

## Final-year project: machine learning for Alzheimer's disease and MCI

*Bachelor's in Computer Science, Bahria University, Lahore · competitive
IGNITE funding*

A CNN classifier for Alzheimer's disease stages from MRI scans (Python,
TensorFlow, Keras), focused on detecting the earliest stages. This project is
the basis of the publication above.

## Statistical modelling of heart-disease data

EDA and feature engineering on a clinical heart-disease dataset, then a
comparison of seven classifiers: logistic regression, SVM, decision trees,
random forests, kNN, naive Bayes and QDA.
